description: LAB-BOUNDED VARIANT for F6 real-lab scenarios 2-4 (#88): identical to the shipped otel-demo-checkout profile except session.max_samples=11 (the smallest budget the loader accepts for a 600 s sustained window at 60 s) so a non-confirming session reaches its real max_samples_exhausted handoff inside the bounded lab run. Recovery definition for the OTel Demo 2.0.2 checkout service on the M1-02 kind lab (kube-state-metrics for deployment state, OTel span metrics for traffic, errors and latency). Every signal is required: F6 step 1 asks for deployment state, request volume, errors, latency, pod health and the dependencies checkout calls before recovery is reported; pod health is read at Deployment level (ready replicas, lowest available replicas inside the window) because a pod name prefix does not prove which workload a pod belongs to. Freshness is judged per signal on the oldest of its series' newest raw sample timestamps (freshness_query = min(timestamp(...)) over the selector), not on the query window, so one stale dependency among eight cannot hide behind the others. Every signal declares a scope (issue #122): the label names under which its selectors carry the subject's namespace and workload; the loader refuses a query that does not select exactly the subject. Span-metric signals bind the namespace through k8s_namespace_name, which the lab's span series carry next to service_name (docs/evidence/m1-02-lab/regression/normal-1/observe-pre.json).
calibration_source: Calibrated 2026-10-07 against the M1-02 step 0 lab observations of 2026-10-06 (docs/evidence/m1-02-lab/regression, 2 locust users): see docs/evidence/m1-02-health-profile/run.md. Frozen before candidate evaluation (C3 section 13).

signals.name: deployment_available_replicas
signals.description: Available replicas of the checkout Deployment (kube-state-metrics). The lab runs spec.replicas=1.

signals.name: request_rate_per_second
signals.description: PlaceOrder server spans per second over the evaluation window; the effective-traffic gate reads this signal. Lab steady state with 2 locust users is about 3.75 orders per 5 minutes (0.0125/s).

signals.name: error_ratio
signals.description: Share of PlaceOrder server spans ending in STATUS_CODE_ERROR. `or vector(0)` keeps a service with no error series from reading as no data; no traffic makes the whole ratio empty, which the traffic gate also catches.

signals.name: latency_p95_milliseconds
signals.description: p95 PlaceOrder server latency from the span-metrics histogram.

signals.name: deployment_ready_replicas
signals.description: Ready replicas of the checkout Deployment (kube-state-metrics kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready). Replaces the pod-level pods_running signal: a pod name prefix cannot prove which workload a pod belongs to, so pod health is read at Deployment level (user decision B, 2026-10-08). The lab runs spec.replicas=1.

signals.name: deployment_available_replicas_min_in_window
signals.description: Lowest number of available replicas of the checkout Deployment at any scrape inside the evaluation window (min_over_time over kube_deployment_status_replicas_available). Replaces the pod-level restart counter: a dip to 0 inside the window is what a restart or crash loop looks like at Deployment level; a restart that comes and goes between two scrapes (60 s in the lab) is not seen, which the restart counter would have shown (user decision B, 2026-10-08).

signals.name: dependency_deployments_available
signals.description: Number of the eight named Deployments checkout depends on (payment, cart and its valkey, product-catalog, currency, shipping, email, flagd) that report at least one available replica. count() over a filtered vector drops a Deployment whose series is missing as well as one with zero replicas, so the value must equal 8 exactly; min() over the same selector would silently ignore a missing series.

signals.name: dependency_error_ratio
signals.description: Share of checkout's outbound (client) spans ending in STATUS_CODE_ERROR, covering every dependency checkout calls.
